screens.instrument: ten 520-cluster mirrored windows, 300 s cap, common MC-LCB control per window; DL random effects
screens.note: Sealed 13:58 ET. A matched-window, COMMON-OPPONENT contrast: each served policy is screened against the same MC-LCB opponents on the same seeds and the arms are differenced, so this is a summary-level estimate, NOT a direct duel and not paired served-vs-served inference. CROSSES ZERO (lower bound -0.002): no resolved difference between run 4's head and production's in served form, and equivalence is NOT established. I2 0%, tau 0, ties 49.7% vs 50.3%. Latency, as the MEAN OF THE TEN PER-WINDOW quantiles (vol_re.py averages window quantiles; it does not pool decision samples): candidate p50 0.10 s / p95 0.16 s, control 0.10 / 0.16. The five-window interim was +0.019 [-0.017, +0.055]. A rough power projection conditional on this effect and variance puts the lower bound near zero around 24 windows total, i.e. about 14 more (~6 h of Perf); that is a projection, not guaranteed resolution, and any extension is a new decision, not queued. data.name: runPV3
data.status: Jerry 17:1x ET asked for 64,000 more clusters. Four 16k stores rather than one 64k run: a manifest is all-or-nothing on the seal, so four stores bound the blast radius and give resume granularity and one seed window each. Queue guards, after Codex found two races on #613: a store waits for its predecessor's DONE line, then takes an atomic mkdir lock held for the run; on Perf it also yields to the whole SCREEN LANE — the lane's own atomic lock and its supervisor process — because a lane runs its windows one at a time and a child-only scan would start in the gap between them. Dry runs write a throwaway seed registry, so they neither pollute the corpus registry nor collide with themselves. ARBITRATION IS START-TIME ONLY: whoever starts first holds the box, so a screen launched while a store is running waits for it (up to ~3.4 h) unless the store is stopped, and --resume continues it. New screens still need coordinating rather than relying on the gates.

models_note: The gen-4 runs are ONE experiment, not four models: the same corpus (all 20 stores, 336,000 deals) and the same evaluation, with a small number of ingredients changed per run. The numbers are the plan's order, not the order they ran — Jerry reordered execution to 1 -> 4 -> 3 -> 2 on 2026-09-21 so the objective was tested before depth. Run 1 is the baseline: gen-3-warm's recipe (residual trunk d4, JS-M1 warm start) on the bigger corpus with HARD targets, the played action as the policy label. Run 4 changes exactly one thing against it, the objective: SOFT targets, the search's own per-candidate values. Runs 2 and 3 are ALSO soft, so the reference for them is RUN 4, not run 1: run 2 changes capacity (residual trunk at depth 6 instead of 4) and run 3 changes architecture AND warm start together (a grid trunk, depth 3 and 44 channels, started from JS-G1 instead of JS-M1). So run 1 vs run 4 isolates the objective, run 4 vs run 2 isolates depth, and run 4 vs run 3 moves two things at once — which is why run 3's read is not attributable to a single ingredient.
